card.name: Pripri
card.tagline: Afro-Dominican accordion-and-balsie dance of the south/east.
card.profile: Pri-pri (pripri) is an Afro-Dominican music-and-dance genre built on three instruments: the one-row diatonic accordion, the guira, and the balsie (a single-headed drum whose player alters pitch with foot pressure). Danced in couples, it is markedly distinct from Cibao merengue: its rhythm is often in 12/8 rather than 4/4. In Villa Mella it is connected to the festivities of the Holy Spirit and the funerary rites of the Cofradia del Espiritu Santo, as well as secular parties. Some researchers group carabine, mangulina and guarapo within a broader 'pri-pri complex' (Ojala.do; Hoy/Museo del Hombre Dominicano).
card.insight: Musician-researcher Tone Vicioso calls pri-pri 'una joya' and notes Marta Ellen Davis's finding that Trujillo rejected pri-pri as too lascivious, championing merengue instead as political propaganda - explaining why pri-pri remained marginal.
card.image_significance: The Dominican juba/balsié complex. A representative image shows percussive hip-and-foot movement in bright street or yard settings — east/southwest, Dominican Republic.
